use_when: You give the tenant a rent concession.

There are items at the property you do not provide. Never list a refrigerator, range, stove, oven, air conditioner or other cooling device you leave at the property, or anything whose failure could affect health or safety.
You want the lease to roll over rather than end on its last day. Keep the renewal term to one year or less, and set reminder and cancellation deadlines you will actually honor.
A condominium declaration covering the property has already been recorded.
The building is covered by Colorado's energy benchmarking law and the utility will not release aggregated data for it without tenant consent.
The property is rural or agricultural.
The property is subject to a recorded environmental covenant or a recorded notice of environmental use restrictions.
The tenant controls the heat and a freeze could damage the property.
The property is in a condominium or planned community whose declaration or bylaws require the association to approve a lease or a tenant.
You have a figure you can justify as your likely daily loss.
You are willing to allow a home business, instead of a flat ban. Leave it out if business use is not permitted.

The property is a single-family home and you own five or fewer single-family rental homes. Leave it out otherwise: it does nothing for any other property, and a false statement in it will be held against you.
The property has shared facilities such as a laundry room, pool, fitness room, clubhouse, elevator or shared yard.
Recommended for any property where a tenant might use a balcony or patio plug-in solar panel.
The tenancy is, or may become, supported by a rental assistance program or housing subsidy.

The tenant can take the property without parking and is choosing to add it. If parking is required, or the property cannot practically be used without it, leave this clause out and include the parking amount in the rent instead.
